targets.rawSql:
SELECT SUM(plant_power_kw)/1000.0 AS "MW"
  FROM v_plant_hourly
 WHERE bucket = (SELECT MAX(bucket) FROM cagg_plant_power_hourly
              WHERE bucket <= $__timeTo()::timestamptz)
   AND region_name = '$region'
   AND plant_id::text LIKE '$plant';

panels.title: Active Faults (answer key)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS "Faults"
  FROM turbine_faults f
  JOIN turbines t ON t.turbine_id = f.turbine_id
  JOIN plants   p ON p.plant_id   = t.plant_id
 -- "Active" AS OF the end of the window, not active right now: started by then
 -- and not yet resolved by then. `resolved_at IS NULL` alone answers a question
 -- about the present, which is wrong on any historical range.
 WHERE f.started_at <= $__timeTo()::timestamptz
   AND (f.resolved_at IS NULL OR f.resolved_at > $__timeTo()::timestamptz)
   AND p.region_name = '$region'
   AND p.plant_id::text LIKE '$plant';

panels.description: Ground truth from turbine_faults. Compare with what the performance ratio led you to suspect — the gap between the two is the value of the monitoring.

panels.title: Plants in $region
panels.description:
Auto-zooms to the selected region (geomap view = 'fit'). Each marker is a PLANT, sized by output and coloured by performance ratio. Use the table below to drill into one.

Zooms to whatever the $region filter selected, by fitting to the PLANTS layer only.

`allLayers: false` plus a named `layer` is the whole fix, and the default is the trap: MapViewConfig defaults `allLayers` to TRUE, so a bare `{id: 'fit'}` fits the union of every layer — including the region-footprint GeoJSON, which spans all six regions worldwide. The map therefore snapped back to a world view on every filter change, no matter which region was selected. Fitting to the marker layer alone makes the extent follow the query.

`maxZoom: 9` keeps a single-plant region at regional scale rather than diving to street level.

WIND VECTOR: the blue arrow at each plant shows which way the wind is currently
blowing, and its LENGTH is the wind speed — 2000 m per m/s, a scale picked for this
panel's zoom so the arrow is legible at the extent shown.

It is drawn by a ROUTE layer, not a rotated marker. The query returns THREE points per
plant — tail upwind, the plant centre, head downwind — and the route layer joins them
into a line with an arrowhead on the forward end. The points are placed with
ST_Project, which is geodesic and takes its azimuth in RADIANS clockwise from north, so
the arrow stays true at any latitude instead of skewing the way a degree-space offset
would.

Grafana's route layer renders ONLY THE FIRST FRAME of its query result (see
`routeLayer.tsx`: `break; // Only the first frame for now!`). So `GROUP BY plant_id`
does NOT give you one arrow per plant — every point from every plant would be strung
into a single zig-zagging line, and partitioning into one frame per plant does not help
either, because frames 2..N are simply dropped. Hence SIX separate route layers (refIds B through G), each
returning exactly one plant via `ORDER BY p.plant_name OFFSET n LIMIT 1`. A region holds
at most six plants (36 sites / 6 regions), so the fan-out is bounded; layers past the
plant count return zero rows and quietly draw nothing.

The bearing is a genuine CIRCULAR MEAN across the plant's turbines, computed from the
unit-vector component sums stored in cagg_wind_hourly — there is no correct way to
average a bearing arithmetically. The tooltip gives both `wind_from_deg` (the
meteorological convention: where the wind comes FROM) and `wind_toward_deg` (where it
is going, which is where the arrowhead points), because an arrow drawn 180 degrees out
looks entirely plausible. `steadiness` is the mean resultant length, 0-1: near 1 the
turbines agreed on the direction, and below 0.01 the arrow is suppressed entirely
rather than pointing somewhere invented.

Cross-read it against `grid_bearing_deg`, also in the tooltip: that is the axis the
turbine grid was laid out on. When the two line up, the array is taking the wind
head-on down its wide spacing and wake losses are at their lowest.

WHY THIS PANEL STAYS PER-PLANT while the plant and turbine views draw one arrow per
turbine: a turbine array is 1-2 km across inside a view spanning hundreds of km. Marker
glyphs are sized in PIXELS, not metres, so per-turbine arrows here would pile into an
illegible blob at each plant. One arrow per plant, with its length encoding speed, is
the readable choice at this zoom.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT p.plant_name,
       p.site_name,
       p.operator,
       p.model,
       ST_Y(p.center_location::geometry) AS latitude,
       ST_X(p.center_location::geometry) AS longitude,
       ROUND((h.plant_power_kw/1000.0)::numeric,2) AS output_mw,
       ROUND(h.performance_ratio_pct::numeric,1)   AS performance_ratio_pct,
       ROUND(h.capacity_factor_pct::numeric,1)     AS capacity_factor_pct,
       h.turbines_reporting                        AS turbines
  FROM plants p
  JOIN v_plant_hourly h ON h.plant_id = p.plant_id AND h.bucket = (SELECT MAX(bucket) FROM cagg_plant_power_hourly
              WHERE bucket <= $__timeTo()::timestamptz)
 WHERE p.region_name = '$region'
   AND p.plant_id::text LIKE '$plant'
 ORDER BY output_mw DESC;

WITH v AS (
  SELECT p.plant_id,
         p.plant_name,
         p.center_location,
         -- Circular mean across the plant's turbines, from the stored unit-vector
         -- component sums. A bearing cannot be averaged arithmetically.
         MOD((DEGREES(ATAN2(SUM(w.dir_sin_sum), SUM(w.dir_cos_sum))) + 360.0)::numeric,
             360.0)::float                                        AS wind_from_deg,
         MOD((DEGREES(ATAN2(SUM(w.dir_sin_sum), SUM(w.dir_cos_sum))) + 540.0)::numeric,
             360.0)::float                                        AS wind_toward_deg,
         SUM(w.avg_free_wind_ms * w.readings) / NULLIF(SUM(w.readings), 0) AS wind_ms,
         SQRT(SUM(w.dir_sin_sum)^2 + SUM(w.dir_cos_sum)^2)
           / NULLIF(SUM(w.readings), 0)                            AS steadiness,
         p.grid_bearing_deg
    FROM cagg_wind_hourly w
    JOIN plants p ON p.plant_id = w.plant_id
   WHERE w.bucket = (SELECT MAX(bucket) FROM cagg_wind_hourly
              WHERE bucket <= $__timeTo()::timestamptz)
     AND p.region_name = '$region'
     AND p.plant_id::text LIKE '$plant'
   GROUP BY p.plant_id, p.plant_name, p.center_location, p.grid_bearing_deg
  -- Suppress the vector when the turbines disagreed about direction: the resultant
  -- collapses and ATAN2(0,0) would return a confident due north.
  HAVING SQRT(SUM(w.dir_sin_sum)^2 + SUM(w.dir_cos_sum)^2) >= 0.01 * SUM(w.readings)
 ORDER BY p.plant_name
 OFFSET 0 LIMIT 1
)
SELECT s.seq                                        AS point_seq,
       v.plant_name,
       ST_Y(g.pt::geometry)                         AS latitude,
       ST_X(g.pt::geometry)                         AS longitude,
       ROUND(v.wind_ms::numeric, 1)                 AS wind_ms,
       ROUND(v.wind_from_deg::numeric, 0)           AS wind_from_deg,
       ROUND(v.wind_toward_deg::numeric, 0)         AS wind_toward_deg,
       ROUND(v.steadiness::numeric, 2)              AS steadiness,
       ROUND(v.grid_bearing_deg::numeric, 0)        AS grid_bearing_deg,
       ROUND((v.wind_ms * 2000.0)::numeric, 0)        AS leg_m
  FROM v
  -- TWO points (one arrowhead; Grafana draws one per SEGMENT), the plant
  -- centre being the midpoint. 1000 m per m/s each way — the scale is tuned to this panel's
  -- zoom, since the LENGTH is the speed and it has to be legible at that extent.
  -- ST_Project is geodesic and takes its
  -- azimuth in RADIANS clockwise from north, which is what a compass bearing is.
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL (VALUES (1), (2)) s(seq)
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT CASE s.seq
             WHEN 1 THEN ST_Project(v.center_location, v.wind_ms * 1000.0,
                                    RADIANS(v.wind_from_deg))    -- tail, upwind
             ELSE        ST_Project(v.center_location, v.wind_ms * 1000.0,
                                    RADIANS(v.wind_toward_deg))  -- head, downwind
           END AS pt
  ) g
 -- Route order IS the line order. Tail to head, so arrow => 1 (forward) puts the
 -- head downwind.
 ORDER BY s.seq;

WITH v AS (

         SQRT(SUM(w.dir_sin_sum)^2 + SUM(w.dir_cos_sum)^2)

       ROUND((h.plant_power_kw/1000.0)::numeric,2)   AS output_mw,
       ROUND(h.capacity_factor_pct::numeric,1)       AS capacity_factor_pct,
       ROUND(h.performance_ratio_pct::numeric,1)     AS performance_ratio_pct,
       ROUND(h.avg_wake_loss_pct::numeric,1)         AS wake_loss_pct,
       ROUND(h.avg_wind_ms::numeric,1)               AS wind_ms,
       h.turbines_reporting                          AS turbines
  FROM v_plant_hourly h
  JOIN plants p ON p.plant_id = h.plant_id
 WHERE h.bucket = (SELECT MAX(bucket) FROM cagg_plant_power_hourly
              WHERE bucket <= $__timeTo()::timestamptz)
   AND h.region_name = '$region'
   AND h.plant_id::text LIKE '$plant'
 ORDER BY output_mw DESC;

panels.title: Production by plant  (tier-selected)
panels.description: Tier-2 read, now zoom-selected across the plant DAILY aggregate, the plant HOURLY aggregate and raw. Watch a whole plant drop together — that is a storm shutdown or a curtailment order, not a turbine fault.

targets.rawSql:
-- One point per day or coarser: the daily rollup already has it.
  SELECT p.plant_name AS metric,
         c.day AS time,
         ROUND((AVG(c.plant_power_kw)/1000.0)::numeric, 3) AS value
    FROM cagg_plant_power_daily c
    JOIN plants p ON p.plant_id = c.plant_id
   WHERE $__timeFilter(c.day)
       AND p.region_name = '$region'
       AND c.plant_id::text LIKE '$plant'
       AND $__interval_ms >= 86400000
   GROUP BY p.plant_name, c.day
  UNION ALL
  -- One point per hour or coarser: the hourly rollup is fine enough.
  SELECT p.plant_name AS metric,
         c.bucket AS time,
         ROUND((AVG(c.plant_power_kw)/1000.0)::numeric, 3) AS value
    FROM cagg_plant_power_hourly c
    JOIN plants p ON p.plant_id = c.plant_id
   WHERE $__timeFilter(c.bucket)
       AND p.region_name = '$region'
       AND c.plant_id::text LIKE '$plant'
       AND $__interval_ms >= 3600000
       AND $__interval_ms <  86400000
   GROUP BY p.plant_name, c.bucket
  UNION ALL
  -- Finer than an hour: only the raw samples carry more detail.
  SELECT p.plant_name AS metric,
         time_bucket('15 minutes', g.time) AS time,
         ROUND((SUM(g.power_kw)/1000.0)::numeric, 3) AS value
    FROM power_generation g
    JOIN plants p ON p.plant_id = g.plant_id
   WHERE $__timeFilter(g.time)
       AND p.region_name = '$region'
       AND g.plant_id::text LIKE '$plant'
       AND $__interval_ms <  3600000
   GROUP BY p.plant_name, time_bucket('15 minutes', g.time)
 ORDER BY time;

panels.title: Plant performance ratio  (tier-selected)
